profiles.name: Ruth Yorke
profiles.excerpt: Ruth Yorke was a stage-trained New York radio actress and linguist whose career stretched from early network drama into Theater Five.
profiles.bio_html:
Ruth Yorke was born in New York City and studied speech and theatre before continuing her training in Vienna with Max Reinhardt. She returned to New York and built a professional career across radio and Broadway.

Yorke appeared on a wide range of dramatic programs and became part of the later Theater Five repertory. Contemporary profiles also noted her fluency in French and German, which complemented the dialect and character work expected of radio actors.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Theater Five performances credited to Yorke, two Columbia Workshop appearances and additional work on The Chase and Top Secret.

profiles.name: Sam Hearn
profiles.excerpt: Sam Hearn was a radio comedy and character performer whose surviving GRH work ranges from The Railroad Hour to major situation comedies.
profiles.bio_html:
Sam Hearn worked in American radio comedy and character performance during the network era. His surviving GRH credits place him in both musical and situation-comedy programs.

Hearn appeared repeatedly on The Railroad Hour and also worked on The Great Gildersleeve, Duffy's Tavern and The Halls of Ivy. That spread reflects a performer comfortable in both scripted comedy and musical-radio settings.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven The Railroad Hour performances credited to Hearn, two The Great Gildersleeve appearances and additional work on Duffy's Tavern and The Halls of Ivy.

profiles.name: Sarah Fussell
profiles.excerpt: Sarah Fussell was a New York radio repertory actress whose surviving work spans adventure, wartime drama, supernatural anthology and science fiction.
profiles.bio_html:
Sarah Fussell belonged to the New York radio repertory during the 1940s and 1950s. Her surviving credits place her across several very different dramatic formats.

Fussell appeared on CBS Radio Workshop, I Love a Mystery, Quiet, Please, X Minus One, Challenge of the Yukon and Words at War. The variety of those programs is the strongest evidence of her professional versatility.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves two performances each on CBS Radio Workshop, I Love a Mystery, Quiet, Please and X Minus One credited to Fussell, plus additional adventure and wartime work.

profiles.name: Tony Hughes
profiles.excerpt: Tony Hughes was a recurring This Is Your FBI actor whose eleven surviving GRH performances document steady work in postwar crime radio.
profiles.bio_html:
Tony Hughes is best documented through This Is Your FBI, the long-running crime series built around dramatized federal investigations.

The program relied on a regular pool of actors who could move among suspects, witnesses, agents and supporting characters while maintaining its restrained documentary tone. Hughes's repeated casting places him inside that working repertory.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 This Is Your FBI performances credited to Hughes, making the series the clear center of his surviving GRH profile.

profiles.name: Walter Burke
profiles.excerpt: Walter Burke was a compact, highly recognizable character actor whose radio work ranged from hard-boiled detective stories to anthology drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Walter Burke built a long career as a character actor across radio, stage, film and television. His distinctive voice and compact physical presence later made him a familiar screen supporting player.

Radio used Burke in detective and dramatic programs including Let George Do It and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, along with anthology work on Escape, NBC University Theater and Words at War.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves four performances each on Let George Do It and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar credited to Burke, plus additional anthology appearances.

profiles.name: William Royal
profiles.excerpt: William Royal was a supporting radio actor whose surviving GRH work is divided between Lux Radio Theatre and Dr. Christian.
profiles.bio_html:
William Royal is best documented through the surviving broadcasts of Lux Radio Theatre and Dr. Christian. Personal biographical detail is limited, so his profile stays anchored to the professional record.

The two series placed actors in very different settings: Hollywood feature-film adaptations on Lux and small-town medical drama on Dr. Christian. Royal's repeated casting across both shows demonstrates dependable supporting work.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Royal and five Dr. Christian appearances.

profiles.name: Ann Thomas
profiles.excerpt: Ann Thomas was a New York radio repertory actress whose surviving work is strongest in The Chase and X Minus One.
profiles.bio_html:
Ann Thomas worked in the New York radio repertory during the postwar network years. Her surviving credits place her in psychological drama, science fiction, experimental anthology and comedy.

Thomas appeared repeatedly on The Chase and X Minus One, with additional work on Columbia Workshop and The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six The Chase performances credited to Thomas, two X Minus One appearances and one broadcast each on Columbia Workshop and The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show.

profiles.name: Athena Lorde
profiles.excerpt: Athena Lorde built a career across stage, radio, film and television, with major microphone work in I Love a Mystery and Quiet Please.
profiles.bio_html:
Athena Lorde was born in 1915 and studied at Columbia University before building a professional career in stage, radio, film and television. She also trained through the American Theatre Wing.

Radio became an important part of her work, including The March of Time, Gang Busters, Young Widder Brown and I Love a Mystery. Her surviving GRH credits also place her in the intimate supernatural repertory of Quiet, Please.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five I Love a Mystery performances credited to Lorde, three Quiet, Please appearances and two Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar broadcasts.

profiles.name: Burford Hampden
profiles.excerpt: Burford Hampden was a radio repertory actor whose surviving work crosses horror, science fiction, anthology and medical drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Burford Hampden is best documented through the surviving radio record, where his name appears across several major dramatic programs.

Hampden worked on The Weird Circle, X Minus One, Columbia Workshop, Dr. Christian, Matinee Theater and Stroke of Fate. That spread places him across horror, speculative drama, literary anthology and contemporary storytelling.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three The Weird Circle performances credited to Hampden, two X Minus One appearances and additional work across four other dramatic series.

profiles.name: Cecil Roy
profiles.excerpt: Cecil Roy became one of radio’s great vocal chameleons, earning the nickname “The Girl of a Thousand Voices” before later animation work.
profiles.bio_html:
Cecil Roy was born in St. Paul in 1900 and became a major radio character actress during the 1930s and 1940s. Her ability to shift instantly among ages, dialects and character types earned her the nickname “The Girl of a Thousand Voices.”

Roy worked on serials, comedy and dramatic programs and later carried the same vocal flexibility into animation, including the original voice of Little Lulu and work associated with Casper the Friendly Ghost.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Theater Five performances credited to Roy. Her broader radio career also included memorable work on Quiet, Please and numerous earlier network series.
